facts.statement: The genus Aquilolamna contains only one known species, Aquilolamna milarcae, also called the eagle shark.

facts.statement: Aquilolamna is classified in its own family, Aquilolamnidae, which is tentatively assigned to the mackerel sharks.
facts.quote: and it is classified in its own family Aquilolamnidae, which has been tentatively assigned to the mackerel sharks.

facts.statement: Aquilolamna had a torpedo-shaped body with extremely long, winglike pectoral fins that were 1.90 meters wide, wider than its body length of 1.65 meters.
facts.quote: It had a torpedo-shaped body and tail similar to that of most sharks, but also had a pair of extremely long, winglike pectoral fins whose width from tip to tip (1.90 meters) were wider than it was long (1.65 meters).

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Aquilolamna was a planktivorous filter-feeder with a manta ray-like body plan, a trait suggesting convergent evolution.
facts.quote: These, combined with its broad head, have led to the hypothesis that Aquilolamna was a planktivorous filter-feeder, suggesting a form of convergent evolution with a manta ray-like body plan

facts.statement: Aquilolamna was described from a single well-preserved specimen recovered in 2012 from Vallecillo in the state of Nuevo León, Mexico.
facts.quote: It was described from a single extremely well-preserved specimen, containing a fully-preserved skeleton and potential skin impressions, recovered in 2012 by an unknown quarry worker in Vallecillo in the Mexican state of Nuevo León.

facts.statement: The species Aquilolamna was formally described in 2021.

facts.statement: The description of Aquilolamna was controversial because the authors claimed the fossil was in a public museum, but it was actually in the private collection of politician Mauricio Fernández Garza.

facts.statement: The authors of the description were accused of scientific colonialism for failing to collaborate with local paleontologists, which is mandated by Mexico's national regulatory agency.

facts.statement: Other paleontologists have reservations about classifying Aquilolamna within Lamniformes due to its unusual features, suggesting future research is needed.
